messages:
Jordan: throwing out an idea from the meeting: move the canonical list of supported precisions and a tiny set of safety hints into the model manifest so the compiler/runtime can agree. Pros/cons?
Marta: makes sense. I'd like the manifest to include a small, cheap-to-check "quality anchor" (e.g. 16-token embedding vector or 8-token loss signature) so canaries can smoke-test quant paths quickly.
Liu: agree. Also include an estimated cost_delta and latency_delta per precision so product can show tradeoffs in the console.
Jordan: for customer overrides we can expose allowed_overrides and an overrides_allowed_until timestamp to give ops a deprecation window. Overrides validated at runtime vs manifest bounds.
Marta: streaming concern: if we fallback mid-stream we break many clients. Option A: don't regenerate, just switch precision for subsequent tokens and emit a warning. Option B: offer an opt-in regenerate flag clients can request.
Liu: prefer Option B as default off. Also add a "soft-correct" mode: do a background corrective pass and append a short clarification rather than full regen. Less disruptive.
Jordan: we'll need manifest signing, manifest_version, and validation_artifact_hash to tie CI evaluation to the manifest. For Dedicated/Private manifests must be accepted via admin API.
ops-bot: RFC created: /rfc/manifest-precision-smoke-anchors-v1 reviewers: Jordan, Marta, Liu
